chunks: 4024 - Jamil ibn Darraj narrated from a man who said:

I said to Abu Abdullah عليه السلام: "May Allah rectify you. We associate with some people from the rural lands, and we give them loans, and they consign their produce to us, so we sell it for them for a fee, and we have a benefit in that."
So he said: "There is no harm in it."
And I only know that he said: "Were it not for what they consign to us from their produce, we would not lend to them."
So he said: "There is no harm in it."

key_terms.الْقَرْضَ: the loan extended to the other party
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permissible
key_terms.مَنْفَعَةٌ: a benefit or gain obtained from the arrangement

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible to benefit from selling a borrower's goods after giving them a loan?
ai.summary: This hadith addresses a financial arrangement in which a loan is given and the lender also benefits by selling the borrower's agricultural produce for a fee. Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام rules that there is no harm in this arrangement, indicating the permissibility of such benefit when it is tied to a separate service and not treated as usurious excess on the loan itself.
